# workflows

## Purpose
GitHub Actions pipelines. `ci.yml` is the push and PR gate (ruff, pytest, container checks, manifest invariants, workflow lint, source secret scan). `docker-build.yml` builds, smoke-tests, scans and publishes the multi-arch Docker image (candidate, verify, promote) and creates the GitHub release on version tags. `security.yml` rescans the stable image `latest` serves weekly. `docs-build.yml` builds the Zensical site, checks links, scans the resolved docs environment and deploys to GitHub Pages.

## Key Files
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `ci.yml` | "CI", on push to every branch, PR to `main` and manual dispatch; only PR runs are cancellable. Jobs: `manifest` (rejects a reintroduced `VERSION`, `requirements*.txt`, `BUILD_INFO`, `docs/requirements-docs.txt`, `mkdocs.yml`, committed `docs/changelog.md`/`docs/license.md`; asserts the version is `X.Y.Z`-shaped; runs the `.github/scripts` tests with `unittest` and `node --test`, and the browser formatting tests of `tests/js` with `npm run test:js`; Node built-ins only, no `npm ci`), `workflows` (actionlint 1.7.12, checksum-verified, plus shellcheck), `zizmor` (1.32.0, reads `.github/zizmor.yml`), `container` (`bash -n` and shellcheck of `docker/entrypoint.sh` and `docker/healthcheck.sh`, `docker build --check`), `stylelint` (`npm ci` and `npm run lint` in `tools/stylelint`, blocking), `check` matrix (`ruff` check + format, `pytest`; installs deps through `tools/pyproject-deps.py`, the private `gillbates-*` git deps through a credential helper fed by `RELEASE_TOKEN`, then `pip check`; sets no `WIREBUDDY_SECRET_KEY` on purpose) and `source-scan` (Trivy CLI v0.70.0 release archive, checksum-verified like actionlint, secret scan, verdict from `trivy_report.py`), plus `layout` (Playwright layout suite from `tests/layout`, **non-blocking** for now, see below). Callable via `workflow_call` with the required secret `RELEASE_TOKEN`: `docker-build.yml` runs it as the release gate |
| `docker-build.yml` | "Docker Multi-Arch Build", triggered by `v*` tags and manual dispatch (which must run from a tag). Jobs: `meta` (validate secrets, derive version/tag/build date from `pyproject.toml`, require the tag to be an ancestor of `main`, resolve the rolling toolchain once, declare the build matrix once via `release_tags.py matrix`, `is_newest` hint via `release_tags.py newest`), `ci` (the gate, after `meta`), `build` per matrix arch (buildx with the BuildKit secret `python_libraries_token`, smoke test master and node mode, record toolchain versions, Trivy CRITICAL/HIGH with `.trivyignore` and `list-all-pkgs` plus `trivy_report.py` coverage proof and `--expect-ref` on the scanned image, push `<version>-<arch>` and record the digest from the push output), `create-manifest` (`toolchain_parity.py` gate, then `candidate-<version>-<run_id>-<run_attempt>` index from the digests, read back and verified), `promote` (re-verifies the candidate, lists Docker Hub again and decides `is_newest` on that fresh listing, sets the version tag and, for the newest stable release only, `latest`, each read back), `cleanup-arch-tags` (`if: always()` after `meta` succeeded: deletes the fragment tags, the candidate only after a successful promote), `cleanup-dockerhub-tags` (gated on promote's `is_newest`; lists again and refuses to delete when a newer release appeared), `create-release` (`release_notes.py`, then `release_publish.cjs`: draft, Trivy reports as assets, verify names, state, size and SHA-256 (API digest or downloaded bytes) before and after publishing, publish with GitHub `make_latest` following `promote`'s `latest_moved`; on a rerun a published release whose notes differ gets this run's body and reports, swapped in under staging names, so it always names the image `:<version>` serves). Every credential job (`meta`, `build`, `create-manifest`, `promote`, both cleanups, `create-release`) references `environment: release`; the release is created with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `create-release` is the only job with `contents: write`. Build artifacts keep 30 days so reruns find them. All actions SHA-pinned; the Trivy binary is the one the pinned action ships, no `version: latest` |
| `security.yml` | "Security rescan", weekly cron and manual dispatch, read-only (`contents: read`). `resolve` finds the highest published stable version tag, or `latest` itself when a newest prerelease has pruned every stable version tag (`release_tags.py stable-latest`, unauthenticated full listing) and its index and per-platform digests (`release_tags.py resolve`, platform set must equal `EXPECTED_PLATFORMS`, a second list kept equal to the build matrix on purpose); `scan` runs Trivy per platform digest with the release-gate policy and `.trivyignore` from the default branch, verdict via `trivy_report.py` with `--expect-ref` on the platform digest; `report-failure` (the only job with `issues: write`) opens or updates one tracking issue via `failure_issue.py` |
| `docs-build.yml` | "Deploy Documentation", triggered by changes to `docs/**`, `zensical.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `pyproject.toml`, `tools/pyproject-deps.py`, `.trivyignore`, `.github/scripts/**`, the workflow itself, a successful tag-push `workflow_run` of "Docker Multi-Arch Build", weekly cron and manual dispatch. `build` installs the `docs` extra, freezes it as `requirements.txt` artifact, copies CHANGELOG/LICENSE into docs, runs `zensical build --config-file zensical.toml --strict --clean`, checks links with lychee; `security-scan` runs Trivy (`scanners: vuln`) on the frozen file with coverage proof; `deploy` needs both and deploys to Pages from `main` (job concurrency `pages`, never cancelled); `report-failure` opens one tracking issue for a failed scheduled run |

## For AI Agents

### Working In This Directory
- Every workflow starts with a header comment and a `run-name`; every job starts with checkout (`persist-credentials: false`), `setup-python` 3.14 and `python3 .github/scripts/ci_job_setup.py` (agent banner, `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` on `RUNNER_TEMP`).
- No `${{ }}` inside a `run:` body: pass values through `env:`. Logic with branches or parsing belongs in `.github/scripts/` with tests, not inline.
- Third-party actions are pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment. Never invent a SHA; take it from the publisher's release.
- Version comes from `pyproject.toml` (read with `tomllib`), not a standalone file; keep that in sync with the Dockerfile.
- Release pipeline is serialized (`concurrency: docker-release`, no cancel); do not change that.
- `layout` (ci.yml) runs `npm run test:layout` (Node.js 24, Chromium; Firefox and WebKit as extra matrix legs on pull requests only). **Temporary non-blocking phase:** the job has `continue-on-error: true`, so a failure shows as a red job and a warning annotation but leaves the run, and the release gate in `docker-build.yml`, green. Criterion to remove that line: three complete green runs on GitHub Actions; until then a persistently failing test must be fixed, not tolerated. Steps are separate so the log shows what failed: environment check (one login cell on `layout.spec.mjs`, starts the app), self-test (Chromium only), full quick suite (runs only after a green environment check). Results (JUnit, traces, screenshots, server logs) are uploaded for 7 days as `layout-results-<browser>`; traces contain the throwaway instance's random login password, which dies with the instance. The job `changes` (`ui_changes.py`, tested by `test_ui_changes.py`) gates it: it runs for a UI-relevant change (everything under `app/` except `AGENTS.md`, `tests/layout/`, `tests/e2e/run_server.py`, `tools/ci-seed-admin.py`, `tools/pyproject-deps.py`, `package*.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `ci.yml`, `ci_job_setup.py`, `ci_output.py`, `ui_changes.py`; the suite starts the real app, so any backend file can change a page or the login), a `v*` release tag, `workflow_dispatch`, and whenever the comparison base is unknown (first push of a branch, failed `git diff`, failed `changes` job: fail-open). Docs, `docker/`, other tests, other tools and other workflows skip it. No `paths:` filter on the triggers, which would filter every job. A skipped layout job counts as success for the release gate and shows as skipped, never as passed. Keep `PREFIXES` in `ui_changes.py` in step with this list. Python deps come from `tools/pyproject-deps.py` (runtime only) with the same credential-helper pattern as `check`.
- Docs builds use `--strict`: a broken link or anchor fails CI.
- Runner images are **named** (`ubuntu-26.04`, `ubuntu-26.04-arm`), never `ubuntu-latest`. `ubuntu-24.04-arm` is the documented fallback if the arm64 job hits capacity problems. `.github/actionlint.yaml` declares the 26.04 labels for actionlint.
- `is_newest` (no newer release of any kind, prereleases included) is the guard that stops an older tag's re-run from moving `latest` or pruning newer releases. Both are irreversible on Docker Hub; do not weaken it. `promote` and `cleanup-dockerhub-tags` each decide it again on a fresh complete listing (`release_tags.py`); the `meta` value is only a hint. The listing fails closed on any status other than a first-page 404.
- A rerun republishes its own version tag onto the newly verified candidate (the build date changes the digest). This deliberately differs from the sibling projects, which keep the version tag immutable. `create-release` therefore updates an already published release whose notes differ, so its index digest, rollback target and Trivy reports match the republished image.
- `security.yml`'s `EXPECTED_PLATFORMS` must equal the build matrix in `docker-build.yml`'s `meta` job and `ARCHES` in `release_tags.py`; pinned by `.github/scripts/test_workflow_contracts.py`.
- The rolling build inputs (`PYTHON_BASE`, `WIREGUARD_TOOLS_REF`, `APT_CACHE_DATE`) are resolved once in `meta` and passed to both architectures; the parity gate (`toolchain_parity.py`) in `create-manifest` detects a drift, a missing architecture or an empty field.
- The Trivy vulnerability gates (image, rescan, docs dependencies) block on CRITICAL/HIGH with `ignore-unfixed` and `.trivyignore`; a scan that cannot be verified never counts as passed.
- `S607` stays enabled on purpose; the `.github/scripts` helpers resolve `git`/`gh`/`pwsh` with `shutil.which`.

### Testing Requirements
- Workflows cannot run locally; lint them with `actionlint` (reads `.github/actionlint.yaml`) and `zizmor --offline --no-progress .github/workflows`.
- The `unittest` run below includes `test_workflow_contracts.py`, which pins structural contracts no single run notices: platform lists, the version regex in both workflows, the exact set of write permissions, a read-only rescan, fragment cleanup reading its architectures from `meta`, no Trivy result defaulted to zero, the source-scan Trivy checksum, SHA pins with version comments, scan before push login, and the CI gate wiring of the release.
- The individual steps are reproducible (Python 3.14; the helper scripts use 3.14 syntax): `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `pytest`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py'`, `node --test .github/scripts/test_release_publish.cjs`, `npm run test:js`, `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on `docker/entrypoint.sh docker/healthcheck.sh`, `docker build --check -f docker/Dockerfile .`, `zensical build --config-file zensical.toml --strict --clean`.

### Common Patterns
- Minimal `permissions`, per-job `timeout-minutes`, `needs` chains between jobs, `set -euo pipefail` in shell steps.
- Cheap first: `meta` runs before the CI gate in the release.
- `!cancelled()` rather than `success()` where a *skipped* dependency must not suppress a downstream job (see `create-release`).

## Dependencies

### Internal
- `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/entrypoint.sh`, `docker/healthcheck.sh`, `zensical.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `.trivyignore`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tools/pyproject-deps.py`, `.github/scripts/`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `tests/`.

### External
- `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-python`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `actions/download-artifact`, `actions/github-script`, `docker/setup-buildx-action`, `docker/login-action`, Docker Hub, `aquasecurity/trivy-action`, Trivy release archives, `lycheeverse/lychee-action`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`, GitHub Pages.
